You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Seller cover note and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD documents, so clause references follow the Seller's numbering and should be checked against the operative draft.

---

## 1. Headline view

The Seller calls this package "fair and balanced." It is not. Taken one at a time, the individual numbers (cap, basket, time limit) are within or near market range. **The real problem is how the provisions work together.** Four of them combine to remove almost all of our recourse for the problems we already know about:

1. **General disclosure** of the whole data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2).
2. **Buyer knowledge exclusion**, which covers both actual knowledge and anything "discoverable" (cl 8.3).
3. **Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5, and the "unless expressly stated otherwise" default in 12.3/13).
4. **Title, capacity, tax and IP are folded into the general regime.**

Under this package, every known issue would be "disclosed" and "known." That covers Riverlark, Bluefen, Ironquay, the bonuses, the DD-006 incident and Sandbar. We would therefore have **no warranty claim** for any of them. Any residual claim would also be capped at AUD 4.8m, sit behind a AUD 250k deductible, and expire after 18 months.

The Disclosure Letter itself also contradicts the Seller's cover note on several points. **Read the cover note as advocacy, not as a statement of fact:**

| Item | Cover note says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | no final consent, no evidence conditions satisfied (DL 2) |
| Riverlark | release "following Completion" | not repaid, no discharge (DL 3) |
| DD-006 | "not expected to be material" | access, scope and notification obligation not established (DL 6) |
| Sandbar | "ordinary-course" | Seller does *not* state they are ordinary course (DL 8) |
| Title | "evidenced" by register | register is only the source relied on; no verification (DL 10) |

---

## 2. Structural issues (the limitation architecture)

### 2.1 Limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.3/13, 12.8, 20.5)

**Seller position:** Caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to every Claim unless expressly excluded.

**Why it matters:** As drafted, the wording would arguably cap or bar:
- specific indemnities, including the existing Ironquay indemnity;
- tax indemnity claims;
- leakage claims and completion-accounts or price-adjustment amounts;
- breach of pre-completion covenants and completion obligations;
- fraud, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment.

The non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording also aims to shut out claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18). Fraud cannot be fully contracted out of in any event, but we should not leave the point arguable.

**Push back:**
- Reverse the default. Limitations in cl 12 apply **only to general Warranty Claims**.
- Add express carve-outs from all limitations for:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or concealment by the Seller or its representatives (including Company management acting before Completion);
  - Fundamental Warranties, the Tax Indemnity and specific indemnities (which get their own regime: see 2.2 and section 3);
  - leakage, price adjustment, covenant breaches and completion deliverables.
- Non-reliance must not exclude liability for the Warranties, the Disclosure Letter, or fraud.

### 2.2 Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limit

**Seller position:** The same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."

**Why it matters:** Title and capacity are the core of what we are paying for. If the shares are not validly owned, unencumbered and fully issued, the whole AUD 24m is at risk. A AUD 4.8m cap and an 18-month limit are not acceptable for title.

**Push back:**
- Cap at **100% of the purchase price**.
- Time limit of **at least 6 years** (aligned with the NSW limitation period for contract), with no de minimis or basket.
- Not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.

### 2.3 Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)

**Why it matters:** The Seller's own DL 10 concedes the register is simply "the source relied on." It is not verification. A register on its own does not exclude:
- unregistered issues or transfers;
- options, convertible notes, SAFEs or ESOP entitlements;
- shareholder agreement pre-emption rights;
- security over the shares (including any Riverlark security over Seller's shares);
- discrepancies with ASIC records.

**Push back:**
- Full title warranty package: legal and beneficial ownership, fully paid, no Encumbrances, no options or convertibles, no rights to call for issue of shares, and valid issue history.
- Our own reconciliation of the register against ASIC searches, PPSR searches (against both the Seller and the Company) and the constitution and shareholder agreement.
- Completion deliverables: executed transfers, share certificates or lost-certificate indemnities, any pre-emption waivers, and PPSR releases.

### 2.4 General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2, Schedule 7)

**Seller position:** Everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, is disclosed against all warranties.

**Why it matters:** This converts our due diligence exercise into a waiver. We would also be bearing the risk of any document in the data room whose significance is not obvious on its face.

**Push back:**
- Delete general disclosure of the data room and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- At most, accept disclosure of the specific documents listed in the Disclosure Letter, and only to the extent **fairly disclosed**. That means with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and *financial effect* of the matter.
- Disclosure qualifies Warranties only. It never qualifies Fundamental Warranties, the Tax Indemnity or specific indemnities.
- No updating or supplemental disclosure between signing and Completion may cure a breach. If one is offered, it should trigger only a Buyer termination right.
- Provide that DL 1.4 (non-admission) and DL 11 (reservation) do not dilute the specific disclosures. In particular, the Seller cannot rely on a disclosure as "fair" while also declining to say whether anything is required or material.

### 2.5 Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)

**Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records.

**Why it matters:**
- This is a constructive-knowledge exclusion and is broader than general disclosure.
- It imputes our advisers' knowledge to us.
- Read literally, it would defeat the specific indemnities we need for matters we already know about, which is exactly why those indemnities exist.

**Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. Replace it with an express provision that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or by any knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. Our fallback position is *actual* knowledge of named individual deal team members only, and never applied to Fundamental Warranties, tax or indemnities.

### 2.6 Cap, de minimis and basket (cl 12.1–12.2)

| Term | Seller | Comment | Buyer ask |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Within market for a non-W&I deal | Accept 20–30%, *provided* the carve-outs above are agreed. Otherwise hold out for higher. |
| De minimis | AUD 25k (~0.1%) | Broadly market | Accept, but aggregate claims arising from the same or related facts |
| Basket | AUD 250k (~1.04%), **excess only** (deductible) | The deductible structure is the main issue | **Tipping basket**: once exceeded, recover from dollar one. Threshold at 0.5–1% (AUD 120k–240k). |
| Time limit | 18 months | Market for general warranties | Accept 18–24 months for general. Tax 5–7 years (to cover ATO amendment periods plus a buffer). Fundamental 6+ years. |

**Consider warranty and indemnity (W&I) insurance.** If we take a W&I policy, a lower seller cap becomes more acceptable. However, known issues (all of section 3) will be excluded from W&I cover. That makes the specific indemnities and escrow below non-negotiable either way.

### 2.7 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

**Push back:**
- **Tax:** a standalone dollar-for-dollar tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and PAYG on the DD-005 bonuses). It should be capped at 100% of price, last at least 5–7 years, and not be subject to the de minimis, basket or disclosure. Add conduct-of-claims provisions.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay chain-of-title gap, the IP warranties should at minimum sit outside the general basket. Ideally they should have an elevated cap (for example 50–100%) and a 3-year time limit.

---

## 3. Specific known issues

### 3.1 Bluefen: change-control consent (≈30% of FY26 revenue)

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Why it matters:**
- Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of revenue (around 30%), so it drives a material part of our valuation.
- DD-002 cl 11.3 attaches *conditions* to consent, and DL 2 confirms there is no evidence those conditions are satisfied.
- A bare "written consent" could be conditional, could carry adverse amendments (price, term, termination for convenience), or could leave the Company in default under 11.3.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.

**Push back:**
- **Condition precedent:** an unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or a consent on terms satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably), with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen. No amendment to the Bluefen contract without Buyer consent.
- **Buyer-only waiver.** The Seller cannot deem the condition satisfied.
- Upgrade to **all reasonable endeavours**, with Buyer participation in engagement with Bluefen.
- Long-stop date with a Buyer walk-away right.
- Consider protection for the period after Completion, such as an escrow or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volumes within an agreed period (for example 12 months) for a reason linked to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (≈AUD 3.2m outstanding)

**Seller position:** Release "to be provided following Completion."

**Why it matters:**
- This is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis.
- The change-of-control clause (DD-003 cl 8.1) is likely to trigger at Completion. It could cause a default or acceleration, and possibly cross-defaults, against a company we now own.
- Until discharge under cl 9.2, the Company's assets, and possibly the shares, stay encumbered.
- A promise to deliver a release after Completion leaves us chasing the Seller once we have already paid.

**Push back:**
- Repay at Completion out of the purchase price, as a line item in the funds flow paid directly to Riverlark.
- **Completion deliverables:** a payoff letter confirming the exact payoff amount (including break costs and accrued interest); an executed deed of release; PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days, backed by an irrevocable authority); and return of any title documents.
- The full payoff amount is treated as Debt in the price mechanics.
- Seller indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability.

### 3.3 DD-005 completion bonuses (AUD 420,000)

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller"; not itemised in the funds flow.

**Why it matters:** These are almost certainly the *Company's* obligations as employer, not the Seller's. Unless they are dealt with in the funds flow, we inherit them at full value, together with on-costs. DL 5 expressly declines to say whether payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs apply. Our estimate is that the true cost is materially above AUD 420k once those are included. The "continued employment" conditions also need clarifying. If any portion vests after Completion, the cost could fall on us post-Completion.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses plus all associated on-costs (employer superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation, and any PAYG withholding mechanics) as **Transaction Expenses / Debt-like items** deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the Seller's proceeds.
- Specific indemnity outside the limitations.
- Obtain the bonus letters and confirm the exact vesting conditions and any amounts payable after Completion. Any retention we want to keep should be negotiated as *our* arrangement, not inherited.

### 3.4 Ironquay: SOW3 IP and the AUD 180,000 open payment

**Seller position:** The existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment, which the Seller says is adequate.

**Why it matters:** The real risk is **IP ownership**, not the AUD 180k. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials only passes on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180k open, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The Company may therefore not own IP that may be integral to its product. That exposes us to:
- infringement claims;
- injunctions;
- re-development costs;
- customer warranty breaches;
- leverage for Ironquay in negotiations.

An indemnity limited to the fee does not address any of these.

**Push back:**
- **CP or Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay covering all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents where relevant.
- If this cannot be obtained before Completion, an **expanded specific indemnity** covering all Loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to, or right to use, Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs, and customer claims. It should sit outside the cap, basket, time limit, disclosure and knowledge exclusions, and be backed by escrow.
- Confirm whether SOW1, SOW2 or any later SOWs carry the same retention-of-title mechanism.

### 3.5 DD-006 export / privacy incident (~1,240 records)

**Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.

**Why it matters:**
- A download link sent to an unintended external address, involving names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, is a potential eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
- Where an entity suspects an eligible data breach, it must carry out an assessment and is generally expected to complete it within 30 days. The incident was known by at least 22 September 2026. Depending on when the Company first became aware, that window **may already have passed**. A failure to assess or notify is itself a compliance exposure.
- Penalty exposure under the Privacy Act regime is significant. There may also be contractual notification obligations to customers, potentially including Bluefen, which interacts with 3.1.
- DL 6 confirms nothing has been established: not access, not scope, and not whether notification is required.

**Push back:**
- **Immediate information request:** incident timeline (date of awareness), the investigation or forensic report, access logs for the link, whether the link has been revoked, the notification analysis, any OAIC or customer correspondence, and customer contract notification clauses.
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Company completes the assessment promptly with Buyer input and makes any required notifications. No admissions or regulator engagement without Buyer consultation.
- **Specific indemnity:** regulatory penalties (to the extent lawfully indemnifiable), investigation and notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and remediation. It should sit outside all limitations and be backed by escrow.
- Warranty that there are no other privacy or security incidents.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Why it matters:** DL 8 asks us to read DD-008 and DD-011 "together for timing/scope," and the Seller *declines* to state they are ordinary course. We see three identical renewals that are "related." That pattern is consistent with a single commitment being split to fall below an approval or conduct-of-business threshold. If the renewals were entered into close to signing or Completion, or with a related party, they may also be leakage.

**Push back:**
- Information request on the dates, term, termination rights, prepayment or accrual position, whether Sandbar is a related party, and internal approvals.
- Aggregate related transactions in the conduct-of-business covenants so they cannot be split below thresholds.
- If any renewal is not genuinely needed or not ordinary course, require termination at the Seller's cost before Completion, or a price adjustment or specific indemnity.
- If Sandbar is a Seller affiliate, treat payments as Leakage.
- Ensure any accrued or prepaid amounts are correctly reflected in completion accounts or net debt.

### 3.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower risk, but verify

The Seller's characterisation is plausible: the lease requires notification rather than consent, and the Mossvale restriction covers assignment rather than change of control. We should still **check this ourselves rather than rely on DL 1.4/11 wording.** In particular, check whether "assignment" in DD-009 is defined to include change of control.

- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or post-Completion covenant.
- Obtain a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right other than Bluefen and Riverlark.

---

## 4. Indicative known-issue exposure

| Item | Indicative amount | Recovery under Seller's package |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m | Nil if treated as disclosed or known |
| DD-005 bonuses + on-costs | AUD 420k + on-costs | Nil ("matter for Seller" but sits in Company) |
| Sandbar renewals | AUD 330k | Nil |
| Ironquay fee + IP title | AUD 180k + unquantified IP risk | Fee-only indemnity, possibly capped |
| DD-006 incident | Unquantified (regulatory, notification, claims) | Nil |
| Bluefen | ~AUD 3.6m annual revenue at risk | No protection beyond a weak CP |

Quantifiable items alone come to **roughly AUD 4.1m or more**, before Bluefen, IP and privacy exposures. That is about 17% of the price.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1: deal-critical (reject outright)**
1. **Limit the limitations.** Caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to general Warranty Claims only. Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, Fundamental Warranties, tax, specific indemnities, leakage and covenant or completion obligations.
2. **Fundamental warranties:** cap at 100% of price, 6+ years, no thresholds, not qualified by disclosure or knowledge. Verify title independently (ASIC and PPSR searches, constitution and shareholder agreement, no options or convertibles). The register alone is not enough.
3. **Delete general disclosure** (data room and public records). Only specific, fair disclosure; no cure by updated disclosure.
4. **Delete the Buyer knowledge exclusion** (cl 8.3). Replace with an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by investigation or knowledge.
5. **Riverlark:** repay at Completion from proceeds, with payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharges as Completion deliverables. Treat as Debt.
6. **Bluefen:** unconditional consent with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied as a Buyer-only waivable CP, all reasonable endeavours, long-stop walk-away, and consider post-Completion revenue protection.

**Priority 2: specific indemnities, price and escrow**

7. **DD-005 bonuses:** deduct the bonuses plus all on-costs from the price as Transaction Expenses, paid through payroll. Add an indemnity.
8. **Ironquay:** payment and confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable. Otherwise, a broad IP title indemnity outside the limitations.
9. **DD-006:** urgent information request, a pre-Completion assessment and notification covenant, and a broad specific indemnity.
10. **Escrow or retention:** negotiate an escrow (indicatively AUD 1.5–2.5m, about 6–10% of price, for 12–24 months) to secure the Ironquay, DD-006 and Bluefen-related protections.
11. **Sandbar:** diligence the related renewals, aggregate thresholds in the conduct covenants, and treat as Leakage or adjust price if not ordinary course or if a related party.
12. **Standalone tax indemnity:** 100% cap, 5–7 years, covering payroll tax and super on the bonuses.

**Priority 3: commercial terms (negotiable)**

13. Cap of 20–30% for general warranties is acceptable *if* items 1–4 are won.
14. **Tipping basket** at 0.5–1%. De minimis of AUD 25k is acceptable, with aggregation of related claims.
15. General warranty period of 18–24 months is acceptable. IP warranties should have an elevated cap and a longer period.
16. Lease and Mossvale: verify independently. Add a no-other-change-of-control warranty.
17. Consider **W&I insurance** for unknown risks. Note it will not cover the known issues above, so items 5–12 must be dealt with in the SPA regardless.

**Immediate information requests to the Seller:**
- Bluefen consent correspondence and cl 11.3 status;
- Riverlark payoff figure and break costs;
- bonus letters and on-cost calculation;
- Ironquay payment status, all SOWs, and willingness to sign a confirmatory assignment;
- DD-006 timeline, investigation report, link access logs and notification analysis;
- Sandbar contracts, dates, approvals and related-party status;
- full capitalisation table, plus confirmation of no options, convertibles or share security.

*Clause references should be checked against the operative SPA draft before the mark-up is issued. Privacy, tax and employment points should be confirmed with specialist advisers.*
